overview: One is a vector force-per-charge quantity; the other is a scalar energy-per-charge quantity, and the two are linked by a gradient relationship.
genZNote: Electric field is the vector doing the pushing; potential is just the scalar scorecard of position.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Force experienced per unit positive test charge at a point.
aspects.valueB: Work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to that point.

aspects.label: Zero Value Implication
aspects.valueA: Zero field means no force on a charge there, but potential can still be non-zero (e.g. inside a charged shell).
aspects.valueB: Zero potential doesn't necessarily mean zero field at that point.
